P1.findings_md:
Weighting: 25% | Peer median: 3.30 | Gap: −0.34 | Strengths: Governance (3.51), Culture (3.51) | Development areas: Digital Strategy (2.46), Innovation (2.34)
Pillar 1 is a study in institutional governance at its best — and strategic articulation at its weakest. Odlum Brown has built genuine governance and culture infrastructure that exceeds peer median (: 3.51 vs. 3.25;: 3.51 vs. 3.50) while struggling to formalise the digital strategy and innovation management frameworks that would anchor the firm's 2025 leadership transition. [E-088,E-012]
P1.heading: 6.1 Pillar 1 — Strategy, Governance & Culture  |  2.96 / 5.00  |  M3

P2.findings_md:
Weighting: 30% (highest) | Peer median: 3.06 | Gap: −0.95 (largest pillar gap) | All 4 categories below peer median | Indeed sentiment cap (3.3/5) applied
Pillar 2 is the most commercially urgent pillar in OB's assessment — and the one where the evidence is most unambiguous. All four P2 categories score below peer median. The Indeed sentiment cap of 3.3/5 applies a level 2.5 ceiling across all P2 categories, but in most cases this cap is not the binding constraint — the underlying architectural absences (no mobile app, no marketing automation, no integrated CRM) are the true ceiling. The −0.95 pillar gap against peers with a 30% Weighting is the single largest contributor to OB's 0.39-point overall deficit. [E-012,E-025,E-030]
P2.heading: 6.2 Pillar 2 — Customer Experience  |  2.11 / 5.00  |  M2

P3.findings_md:
Weighting: 20% | Peer median: 3.19 | Gap: +0.14 (OB above peer median) | Strengths: Compliance (3.98), Operational Risk (3.52) | Development area: Process Automation (2.40)
Pillar 3 is OB's strongest pillar and the one where its institutional tenure and governance culture create measurable differentiation. Two of four P3 categories materially exceed peer median (: 3.98, +0.73;: 3.52, +0.27). The single P3 development area — Process Automation (2.40, −0.60) — is directly caused by the Broadridge-Salesforce integration gap documented in ISS-002, and is the precise gap that MuleSoft (R-02) closes. [E-093,E-112,E-012]
P3.heading: 6.3 Pillar 3 — Operations, Risk & Compliance  |  3.33 / 5.00  |  M3

P4.findings_md:
Weighting: 25% | Peer median: 3.06 | Gap: −0.18 | Strengths: Cybersecurity (4.05), Cloud Architecture (3.52) | Development areas: Data Architecture (1.99), Analytics (1.98)
Pillar 4 tells the Infrastructure Paradox story. OB has invested in genuinely best-practice infrastructure ( Cybersecurity: 4.05, +0.80 vs. peers; Cloud Architecture: 3.52, +0.52) that makes Salesforce cloud deployment simpler and safer than at most comparable independent dealers. Yet the application layer above that foundation ( Data Architecture: 1.99; Analytics: 1.98) is critically underdeveloped — both scoring 1.99-2.0 against a peer median of 3.00. [E-093,E-091,E-019]

narrative.recommendations_md:
6 recommendations | All technologies validated absent before inclusion | No investment amounts, estimates, or timelines | Each aligned to OB's 2025 strategic objectives
The following six recommendations address the confirmed capability gaps identified in Sections 6-8. Each recommendation maps to one of OB's seven 2025 strategic objectives, cites specific evidence for the root cause, confirms the technology is not currently deployed, and identifies the named economic buyer. The recommendations are presented in dependency sequence — R-01 (FSC) establishes the financial services data model that R-03, R-05, and R-06 require; R-02 (MuleSoft) establishes the API layer that R-04 (Data Cloud) requires.
